NAMED, NOT UPHELD — the mechanical rule never proposed this one and could not. `namesake.choose` weighs the FIRST forename token, and the register prints this man's MIDDLE name in the forename's place, so GURTREY was put to all the Blanchards the town holds and named none of them. What names him is the town's own directory: Fergus 1843 prints 'Blanchard, Francis Gurtrey, capitalist, res 45 Wells [died, Brooklyn, N.Y., 1872.]' — forename Francis, middle name Gurtrey — and Fergus 1839 and Norris 1844 print the same man 'Francis G.' GURTREY is that middle name, and the card carries it as Gantry because the poll of 1834 prints him 'Blanchard, F. Gantry'. THE REGISTER PROVES ITS OWN HABIT HERE, AT ONE SALE. The six GURTREY rows (purchase nos 0367525-0367530, volume 817 page 027) and the three F G rows (0376893-0376895, volume 818 page 010) are the SAME school section — section 16, T39N R14E, type SC — entered on 22 and 24 October 1833, the days the school section was sold off by lot and by block. One buyer, one auction, two volumes of the register, two renderings of one name; the domain's README already records this habit under T-0990, where HUNTER E E and HUNTER EDWARD E are the same 80 acres of section 13 on the same day at the same price. WHAT IS NOT NAMED BY IT. The town's other documented Blanchard is W. G. Blanchard, the house-and-land agent of the Democrat of 9 July 1834, and his forename initial is W: he is refused on the same ground the crosswalk refuses him against every other Blanchard reading. Joseph Blanchard the blacksmith is a man of the directories and not an 1835 resident. Nothing reached prints a second Gurtrey Blanchard anywhere. AND IT IS STILL A PURCHASE. The Residence column reads UNKNOWN on all six rows, so this names a buyer and never an occupant, and it places nobody on that ground. The six rows are lot 1 of block 2, block 21, lot 8 of block 141, block 3, lot 7 of block 82 and lot 1 of block 141 of the school section, $547.00 in all (ls0076-ls0081). Two of them state a price per acre of 3.69 against 0000.00 acres, which is the acreage of the F G row ls0074 standing in the wrong column of the deposit; it is carried as the register has it and read as no acreage at all.
